title: A fixed 18.61-year term reduced annual mean high-water offset forecast error at six US gauges in 1998-2025
abstract: We tested annual mean high-water height above mean sea level at six US gauges. We used fixed NOAA monthly records and fits that use only earlier complete years. A trend model plus a fixed 18.61-year sine and cosine term lowered mean squared error at all six gauges in 1998-2025. The equal mean of gauge reductions was 70.12%, with a conditional 95% five-year block interval of 59.13% to 76.36%. The cycle model beat the last available annual value at five gauges but had 40.67% higher error at The Battery. A reporting-lag check retained a 70.22% gain against its trend reference. Four control periods raised aggregate error. The same term gave only 2.18% mean gain for the average monthly highest-water offset and raised mean sea-level error by 5.29%. Both secondary intervals included zero. These findings support a narrow annual tide-height benchmark. They do not establish flood-prediction skill or a new physical cause. Six selected gauges, source revisions, missing annual records, simple model forms, and only about 1.5 test cycles limit inference. The package contains exact source bytes and hashes, code, all forecasts and block draws, figures, a separate arithmetic audit, and an exact offline repeat.
